summary.text: Mark DeSaulnier is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 10th Congressional District, which covers much of Contra Costa County and part of Alameda County. A former Bay Area restaurant owner, he served on the Contra Costa County Board of Supervisors, as mayor of Concord, and in the California Assembly and Senate before his election to Congress in 2014. He sits on the Education and Workforce and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and is Ranking Member of the House Ethics Committee; he is running for re-election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Lowell, Massachusetts. Earned a high school diploma from Cranwell Preparatory School and a B.A. in history from the College of the Holy Cross in 1974; his first job, per his Ballotpedia survey, was as a deputy probation officer at Boston Juvenile Court during college.

According to his official biography, he moved to California in the early 1970s and over the next 35 years owned and managed several Bay Area restaurants, including Henry Africa's in San Francisco, Santa Fe Bar and Grill in Berkeley, and TR's in Concord. He was a member of the Teamsters and the Hotel Employees and Restaurant Employees unions.

Held local office as a member of the Contra Costa County Board of Supervisors and as mayor of Concord, and served on the California Air Resources Board (1997-2006), according to his campaign website, as well as the Bay Area Air Quality Management District and the Metropolitan Transportation Commission.

Served in the California State Assembly (District 11, 2006-2008) and the California State Senate (District 7, 2008-2014). His official biography says he was the first freshman in history to chair the Assembly Transportation Committee and later chaired the Senate Transportation and Housing Committee.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2014, taking office in January 2015, after advancing from the June 2014 primary and winning the general election in what was then the 11th District.

Sits on the Education and Workforce Committee, where he is Ranking Member of the Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions Subcommittee, and on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. Appointed to the House Ethics Committee in the 118th Congress, where he is now Ranking Member; previously served on the Rules Committee, where he was Vice Chair.

His office says he has passed more than 60 legislative efforts in Congress and that 61 of his bills became California law during his time in the state legislature. His office received a Congressional Management Foundation Democracy Award in 2019.
Lives in Concord, where he raised his two sons, according to his official biography; he has also run 23 marathons.
